text.p: These are the leading stories in Zimbabwe's state-owned Herald newspaper on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Forty-three Zimbabwean students, some of them from poor families, leave Harare on Wednesday morning to pursue studies at Fort Hare University in South Africa as beneficiaries of the Presidential Scholarship Programme.

- The scramble for Zimbabwe's second cellular telephone tender is reaching its finale with the government having pruned the bids to four from six for consideration by the tender board. The winner is expected to be known next week.
- The Zimbabwe Electricity Supply Authority has started implementing its rural electrification programme, with 28 new centres already connnected to the grid.

- Mazowe Dam in Zimbabwe's Mashonaland Central province spilled for the first time in more than 10 years on Monday, bringing relief to Mazowe Citrus Estates which takes the bulk of the dam's water to irrigate its fruit.
